Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: review of the Seller's update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall:** This is not a "fair and balanced package". Most of the Seller's "negotiated positions" were never negotiated or agreed, so we should say so in our reply. The package combines a low cap, high thresholds, a short claims period, deemed disclosure and a buyer-knowledge bar. It also applies all of these to every claim, including title and fraud. Together they would leave the Warranties close to worthless. The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the cover note, and its specific admissions give us useful leverage.

## 1. Structural issues (highest priority)

**a. Fraud and misconduct (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).** The limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to "all Claims of any nature". That sweeps in fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Our playbook requires a carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Nobody on our side can waive this. Reject outright.

**b. The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" override (cl 12.3 / 13).** This is the hidden general-regime override the playbook warns about. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and payment covenants into the general limits. Reverse it so the general limits apply only to General Warranty Claims, and each other category has its own regime.

**c. Fundamental/Title warranties on the general cap and time limits.** Reject. Our position is a separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cut title protection.

**d. Deemed disclosure (Schedule 7, Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).** The Seller discloses the entire data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records. We should reject all of this and require specific, fair disclosure against identified Warranties. Two further points:
- Paragraph 1.3 is missing (the letter goes 1.1, 1.2, 1.4). Ask whether text was removed.
- The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, and today is 6 November. We need to know what has changed since, and the Warranties should be brought down to Completion.

**e. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** This is a blanket exclusion covering anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records. Combined with (d), it removes protection for anything in the data room twice over. Delete it. Any fallback qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**f. Why this matters for the specific issues below.** Once a fact is disclosed, it qualifies the Warranties. Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and the DD-006 incident are all disclosed. We therefore cannot rely on warranty claims for them. They need conditions, funds-flow treatment or specific indemnities that sit outside the general limits.

## 2. Commercial terms against the playbook

| Term | Seller | Our starting position | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | The Seller's figure is our conditional fallback. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost, so we cannot accept it. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | 5x our figure, and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. |
| Claims period | 18 months | 24 months | The Seller's period is our fallback, which also needs Frost's written approval. None has been given. |

The thresholds are the bigger problem. A AUD 250,000 deductible with a AUD 25,000 claim floor means several moderate breaches could be wholly unrecoverable. Our reply should counter at the starting positions without hinting at fallbacks. If the team wants to consider either fallback, we first need Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft.

## 3. Deal-specific points

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, around 30% of FY26 revenue).** The Disclosure Letter admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours" and deems the condition satisfied "on delivery" of consent. That is below our standard for a material customer. We should require, as a condition to Completion:
- an effective written consent, and
- evidence that its conditions are satisfied.

A delivered consent that is itself conditional should not count as satisfaction. The condition should be for our benefit only to waive.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m).** The facility has not been repaid and no discharge has been provided. The Seller proposes a release after Completion. We should require:
- a current payout letter,
- direct repayment from Completion funds, and
- effective security releases at Completion.

A post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking plus Frost's approval, and neither exists. Also check the change-control clause (8.1) for any default risk before repayment.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000 plus on-costs).** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but leaves them out of the funds flow, and the disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, super or other on-costs apply. Accept the Seller's statement, but hold them to it. The bonuses and triggered on-costs should be either a specific funds-flow line item or an express seller-funded obligation. The on-costs need to be quantified. The funds flow should not be described as "agreed" until this is resolved.

**Ironquay IP.**
- The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. We should broaden it to cover ownership and assignment of the SOW3 materials, third-party claims and related costs.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure: cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment.
- The AUD 180,000 is unverified in both directions. DD-010 is not bank evidence of non-payment, and there is no receipt in the data room. We should neither assume it is owed nor accept that it is settled.
- Keep this as a separate indemnity outside the general limits.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006).** The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". We should not adopt that wording, and we should equally not assume a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any dollar figure. The Disclosure Letter itself says access, scope and notification are unresolved. The protections we need are:
- log preservation,
- a proper investigation,
- regular updates to us, and
- cooperation and a say in any regulatory step.

Ask for the current status, since the disclosure is dated 22 September.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000, three at AUD 110,000).** Calling them "ordinary-course" is an unverified characterisation, and the letter does not say whether they are committed, terminable or accrued. We should assess them from DD-008 and DD-011 and ask for the terms. We should not push for Debt classification or a price deduction unless the assessment supports it, and we should not accept the Seller's label as a deemed fact.

**Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime". They are not. Both remain open. Our reply should say so, keep Tax and IP as separate categories, and not accept any general-regime default. We should also not demand unlimited liability or treat anything as resolved.

**Title.** DD-012 is the Company's own share register. It is a supplied internal source, not independent proof, and the Disclosure Letter (para 10) concedes we have not verified title. We should require independent evidence of:
- ownership,
- encumbrances (charges, PPSR and other registrations), and
- the Seller's authority and capacity.

**Lower priority.** The lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) disclosures say what the documents "do not state". That is not confirmation that no consent or notice is needed on a change of ownership. We should review the clauses ourselves, including any deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "negotiated positions" framing.** State that nothing is agreed and all points are reserved.
2. **Counter at playbook starting positions:** 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24 months. Do not reveal or use the fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority.
3. **Rewrite the limitation architecture:** general limits apply only to General Warranty Claims. Title and fundamental claims get a separate regime (100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar). Tax, IP, indemnities and covenants stay separate.
4. **Add the fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
5. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure** and delete cl 8.3. Any knowledge qualifier must use named Seller persons and reasonable enquiry, and never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
6. **Make Bluefen a Completion condition:** effective consent plus evidence its conditions are met.
7. **Riverlark:** current payout, repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion.
8. **Funds flow:** show the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus on-costs as a line item or an express seller-funded obligation.
9. **Ironquay:** a broader specific indemnity, with the SOW3 cure preserved.
10. **DD-006:** preserve logs, investigate and provide updates, without conceding any characterisation.
11. **Sandbar:** diligence only, with no automatic price deduction.
12. **Title:** require independent verification and do not rely on DD-012.
13. **Information requests:** the missing paragraph 1.3, data room changes since 22 September, the DD-006 status, the Bluefen consent conditions, a Riverlark payout figure, the on-costs calculation, the Ironquay payment evidence, and the lease and Mossvale clause text.

I can turn this into a draft mark-up or a response letter to the Seller's counsel if that would help.
